title: Provision-to-ready alert tuning notes (early rollout)
body:
Context
- Staged rollout: us-east / A100 Dedicated pool only (feature flag ON for a single pool). Goal is to enable paging only once we have stable metric cardinality + a week of baseline.
- This doc is SRE working notes for alert thresholds (page vs ticket), expected noise sources, and what we learned during week 1.

Where to look (dashboards + the “metrics page”)
- Grafana folder: “Provision-to-Ready” (from observability-pack/pr-812)
  - Dashboard: Provision-to-ready overview (SLO tiles + current state counts)
  - Dashboard: Step breakdown (latency P50/P95 by step)
  - Dashboard: Failure heatmap (failure rate by step x region x gpu_type)
  - Dashboard: Quarantine (quarantined node counts + top quarantine reasons)
  - Dashboard: Validation flake rate (per validation check; intended to catch NCCL/network jitter)
- Fleet readiness service UI endpoint (internal) for drill-down:
  - /internal/fleet/readiness/summary (counts by state + top failures) (ref redwood/pr-18460)
  - Per-node details: validation artifacts/log pointers (ref redwood/pr-18429)

Metric naming assumptions (verify in dashboard)
- Note: exact metric names can drift; defer to the dashboard panels as source-of-truth. What we’re alerting on logically:
  1) Time-to-ready latency: (allocated -> ready) distributions
  2) Provision-to-ready success rate (node reaches Ready within time window)
  3) Step failure rates (esp. kubelet join, driver parity, NCCL smoke)
  4) State stuckness (nodes stuck in Provisioning/Validating)
  5) Quarantine rate/count (quarantine spike is often the “real incident” even if validations are technically working)

SLOs (current proposal used for tuning)
- Reference: Confluence “provision-to-ready-slo-and-error-budget” (draft as of 2025-10-16)
- For staged rollout we’re using softer thresholds; we’ll tighten once rollout expands beyond us-east/A100.
  - Time-to-ready P50 target: <= 35 minutes (stretch goal <= 25m)
  - Time-to-ready P95 target: <= 90 minutes
  - Success rate (Ready within 2h of allocation): >= 97% (stretch 99%)
  - Error budget policy: during rollout, consume budget without paging unless customer impact or quarantine spike causes capacity loss.

Alerting philosophy (what pages vs what tickets)
- Paging should correlate with either:
  - Customer impact in the next 1–2 hours (capacity shortfall / Dedicated pool expansion blocked)
  - A widespread regression likely to get worse (e.g., image channel issue, kubelet join failure across nodes)
- Ticket alerts are for:
  - Degraded metrics without immediate capacity impact
  - Known flaky validations (NCCL/network jitter) until we stabilize
  - SLO burn that is slow/steady and better handled in business hours

Proposed alert rules (v0.3 after week-1 tuning)

A) Time-to-ready latency (allocated -> ready)
- Ticket: P95 time-to-ready > 120m for 2 consecutive 30m windows (region=us-east, gpu=A100, pool_type=dedicated)
  - Rationale: catches slowdowns but avoids paging when the queue is just “busy.”
- Page: P95 time-to-ready > 180m for 2 consecutive 15m windows AND allocated_count >= 10 in same window
  - Extra guard: only page when there’s enough sample size; otherwise it’s a single bad node.
  - Notes: during low volume, latency percentiles are unstable; sample-size gating is required.

B) Success rate (Ready within 2 hours)
- Ticket: success_rate < 95% over trailing 6h (min 20 nodes)
- Page: success_rate < 90% over trailing 2h (min 20 nodes)
  - Rationale: “<90% for 2h” is effectively a systemic regression.

C) Step failure rate (per-step)
- Ticket: any single step failure_rate > 10% over 1h (min 20 step executions)
- Page: failure_rate > 25% over 30m for any of:
  - kubelet_join
  - driver_parity
  - gpu_health
  - nccl_smoke
  - (min 20 executions)
  - Rationale: these steps dominate “can’t bring up capacity” outcomes.

D) Stuck states (state machine)
- Ticket: nodes_in_state{Validating} > 15 for > 30m
- Page: nodes_in_state{Validating} > 30 for > 20m OR nodes_in_state{Provisioning} > 30 for > 20m
  - Add label filters: region + pool_id (paging should go to owning oncall for that region/pool)
  - Caveat: during a planned bulk expansion, “stuck” may just mean “waiting”; needs correlation with step timings.

E) Quarantine signals
- Ticket: quarantined_nodes increase by > 10 in 2h OR quarantine_rate > 5% in 2h
- Page: quarantined_nodes increase by > 10 in 30m OR quarantine_rate > 15% in 1h
  - Rationale: quarantine spikes can immediately reduce serving capacity, even if provisioning/validation are “working.”
  - Add annotation to page: check whether quarantine policy recently changed (ref redwood/pr-18452).

F) Telemetry health (meta-alerts)
- Ticket only (no page during rollout): missing metrics / ingestion delay
  - If we page for telemetry failures early, we will burn oncall time without direct customer impact.

Routing / ownership
- Primary paging rotation: SRE Oncall (first line triage) + Fleet/Infra secondary (Vanessa’s team) for step-specific regressions.
- If the failure mode is control-plane readiness service (state writes, authz, API failures): page Platform control plane oncall.
- Practical mapping guidance (for the alert annotations):
  - kubelet join / node config baseline -> Infra/Fleet
  - readiness state transitions not updating -> Platform control plane
  - dashboard/metrics ingestion/cardinality -> Observability/SRE

Noise + flake analysis (what happened in week 1)
1) Metric tag/cardinality incident (real)
- Symptom: Prometheus/Grafana panels slowed / alert evaluations spiky. Also saw “too many series” warnings.
- Root cause: per-node identifiers included as tags for step spans/metrics.
- Fix: redwood/pr-18475 removed per-node IDs from tags and updated dashboards.
- Follow-up: keep an explicit “allowed tag set” list in the instrumentation doc; add CI lint if possible.

2) NCCL smoke test flakes (expected, but too noisy)
- Symptom: intermittent nccl_smoke failures clustered at certain times; often self-healed on retry.
- Contributing factors:
  - network jitter during parallel bring-up
  - timeouts too aggressive (esp. when disks/caches cold)
  - occasional contention from other bootstrap tasks
- Mitigations in progress:
  - increase timeout + add structured retry/backoff (ref redwood/pr-18481; Linear ENG-4830)
  - adjust alerting: keep NCCL failure as ticket unless it crosses the >25%/30m paging threshold with min sample.

3) “Validating stuck” false positives at low volume
- Symptom: a single node can make percentiles and stuck counts look bad when total nodes are low.
- Mitigation: add min sample size gates and/or use absolute counts rather than percentiles for paging.

4) Planned rollouts causing alerts (expected)
- When we intentionally bring up 20–40 nodes, step execution volume spikes; this can trip rate-based alerts.
- Mitigation: add a rollout annotation window (manual) and/or use a feature-flag label to suppress pages for the first 30m after enabling a new pool.
  - Action item: define how to programmatically label “rollout in progress” for alert suppression without hiding real regressions.

Paging vs ticket thresholds (current recommendation)
- Enable paging only for quarantine spikes + systemic failures (success_rate < 90% over 2h, step failures > 25% over 30m, or huge stuck counts).
- Everything else starts as ticket during staged rollout, with a weekly review to tighten.

Operational playbook links (for alert annotations)
- Runbook: provision-to-ready failures triage (Confluence)
  - first checks: readiness summary endpoint, step breakdown dashboard, validation artifact logs
  - safe actions: drain -> quarantine -> reimage (in that order unless directed otherwise)
- Game day plan: provision-to-ready gameday scenarios (Confluence)

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm “allocated” timestamp source of truth used by SLI calculation (slo-toolkit/pr-309). We saw a mismatch between infra allocation event time and control-plane allocation record for a subset of nodes.
- Decide whether to page on “P95 time-to-ready burn” vs “failure/quarantine” signals. My current bias: page on quarantine/capacity-loss signals only.
- Confirm that alerts group by pool_id and not instance_id/node_id to avoid cardinality blowups.
- Add a per-pool “expected provisioning volume” (planned expansions) to reduce false positives.

Changelog
- 2025-10-14: initial notes (v0.1) during alert rule drafting
- 2025-10-17: added sample-size gates + moved NCCL failures to ticket by default (v0.2)
- 2025-10-21: updated after metric-cardinality incident + proposed quarantine paging thresholds (v0.3)
